title: رحلة ابن بطوطة (Riḥlat Ibn Baṭṭūṭa)
shelf_note: Arabic printed text of Ibn Battuta's Rihla (India section, executions under the Sultan); belongs in booksbylanguage_arabic. 'published: 1355' is the date of composition, not of this printing.
structure_note: printed_repeats 232 of 532 numbered pages with printed '(٧٠)' on record 378 suggests the scan holds more than one volume/part, each paginated from 1, so repeats and most of the 13 backsteps are pagination restarts rather than defects (a few backsteps may be misread numerals). structure.pages_translated is 0 while the book field says 568 and this page carries a translation: the counter is wrong (E2).

pages.layout: single column of printed naskh, centred page number in parentheses over a rule, two centred section headings between ornaments

ocr_errors.problem: 'rebelled' misread as 'feared'; changes the sense (translation follows the image)
'would be pardoned' misread as 'would suffice/enrich'; meaning lost in the OCR

ocr_errors.image: فقال هلا قلت هذا قبل موته
ocr_errors.problem: 'هلا' (why not) dropped, so the Sultan's rebuke reads as a statement

ocr_errors.ocr: قد لبس ثيابه جيل قلنسوة على رأسه
ocr_errors.image: قد لبس ثيابه وجعل قلنسوته على رأسه

ocr_errors.ocr: وحاولا الفرار في بهما أحد أصحابهما
ocr_errors.image: وحاولا الفرار فوشى بهما أحد أصحابهما

other.note: Section headings carry raw centring markup in the English: "-> ❖ Account of his execution of Tughan and his brother ❖ <-"
The translation reads the image where the OCR is wrong ('rose against', 'pardoned', 'Why did you not say this', 'Kanbaya', 'Bakht'), so the two panes disagree; the English is the correct one

items.quote: original: "al-qa'im", the one who rose up

missing.english: word reached the Sultan that Sheikh al-Haydari had prayed for Judge Jalal
missing.why: 'the Sultan' throughout is never identified (Muhammad ibn Tughluq of Delhi); a general reader opening this page does not know whose executions are listed

missing.english: The Sultan then left behind at Kanbaya Sharaf al-Mulk Amir Bakht
missing.why: Kanbaya is Cambay (Khambhat) in Gujarat; the name is unrecognisable without a gloss

book_verdict: The English is a faithful, careful translation that silently corrects several meaning-changing OCR misreads (خاف for خالف, يغني for يعفى, dropped هلا), so the Arabic panel is weaker than the English. Notes are sparse and correct; the only visible blemish is raw '-> ❖ … ❖ <-' markup on the headings.
